name: Lounge & dining room

dimensions.notes: Plan size scaled from the 1:50 survey (±10 cm). 2.42 m was the old ceiling height — the ceiling has since been removed, so the room now rises to the exposed beams/boards. New height to the boards and to the ridge: to measure.

orientation: Double doors at the front onto the front terrace; double doors at the back onto a tiny back terrace

photos.caption: Looking towards the front terrace doors — exposed beams and boards, stepped niche seating on the right

current.summary: Now one open living space, with the old ceiling removed so it opens up into the attic and roof. Double doors at the front onto the front terrace and double doors at the back onto a tiny terrace. Layout today: a sitting area — grey sofa (2.1 m long) facing the TV — and a dining area with a table for 4, plus two built-in cupboards. Walls are white, softly uneven plaster. The angled side wall is built up in white masonry steps: a deep niche used as a daybed/seat, and above it a long ledge with old beam pockets (the sockets where earlier beams sat) and a small high window. A panel of exposed brick sits beside the glazed wooden French doors to the terrace. Floor: large-format grey tiles. Furnishing: the grey sofa with leaf-print cushions, antique wooden bar counter, gilt mirror over a wrought-iron wine-rack console, open shelving on the left. Lighting is a mix: glass-drop chandelier, a black cage pendant on a long flex looped across the beams, a cage wall-light.
keep: Exposed beams and boarded deck — the best feature of the floor
Old beam pockets in the side wall (character; could be lit)
Exposed brick panel by the terrace doors
Stepped masonry niche — make it a proper built-in daybed
Wooden glazed French doors to the terrace
Antique bar counter and gilt mirror
issues: Pendant flex draped and looped across the beams — needs a proper cable route / fixings
Light fittings in three different styles (crystal, black cage, gilt) — pick one family
High ledge currently used for storage boxes — needs a plan (display or concealed storage)
Ceiling removed: check what is above the boards — roof insulation, draughts, condensation (Gratteri winters are cold)
Grey tile + grey sofa read cold against the warm timber

target.concept: DRAFT for discussion — let the timber lead. Keep the walls a warm lime-white with their soft, hand-finished texture so the dark beams, the boards and the brick panel do the talking. Turn the stepped niche into a properly built-in daybed with tailored linen cushions and bolsters; make the high ledge a lit display shelf (ceramics, books) instead of a store. Rationalise the lighting into one warm family (aged brass / natural linen), add uplight onto the boards so the roof volume glows at night, and warm the grey floor with a big flat-weave or kilim rug.
